headline: I Squared Capital buys Indonesian cold-storage and logistics platform Cella
players: I Squared Capital agreed to acquire Cella, an Indonesian industrial logistics and cold-storage platform, from NWP Property and Japan-based CRE, Inc. Cella owns five operational facilities totaling about 231,000 square meters across Greater Jakarta and Surabaya. Terms were not disclosed; the deal is expected to close in Q3 2026.
why_it_matters: The deal gives I Squared a buy-and-build platform in one of Southeast Asia's fastest-growing cold-chain markets, adding to a logistics roster that already includes WOW Logistics, Cube Cold and Royal Cold Storage. It signals sponsors are still finding organic-growth logistics platforms attractive even as capital and headlines skew toward AI power. Watch for follow-on tuck-in acquisitions once the deal closes.
why_you_care: A rival's mid-market logistics platform build in Asia, useful as a comp if MSIP looks at similar buy-and-scale cold-chain or logistics plays.

headline: FTAI Infrastructure Q2: rail hits record revenue, Long Ridge sale to MARA still pending
players: FTAI Infrastructure reported a Q2 2026 net loss of $166.5 million, versus $83.9 million a year earlier, with total debt of about $2.76 billion and negative total equity. The rail segment posted record revenue and Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter, and the company completed its Tidewater Logistics tuck-in acquisition on June 29. The pending $1.52 billion sale of Long Ridge Energy and Power to MARA Holdings, expected to close in Q3, will eliminate $1.16 billion of Long Ridge debt and repay roughly $300 million of other debt.
why_it_matters: The Long Ridge exit meaningfully deleverages FTAI Infrastructure and sharpens its focus on the rail, ports and midstream assets that anchored the original thesis. Rail's record quarter is the clearest read yet on Transtar's underlying earnings power even as headline losses widen on non-cash items. Watch whether the MARA sale closes on schedule and how proceeds get redeployed.
why_you_care: This is the deal he underwrote at Rothschild moving in real time, and the Long Ridge exit and rail strength are worth flagging inside MSIP as a live comp.

headline: Texas Gov. Abbott freezes new data center grid connections pending ERCOT/PUCT audit
players: Governor Greg Abbott directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT to audit all data center projects in the interconnection queue before approving any new grid connections. ERCOT suspended the Batch Zero Large Load classification notices that were due to Transmission/Distribution Service Providers by August 7 and will seek a good-cause exception at PUCT's August 20 meeting. The ERCOT queue had reached roughly 474 GW as of late July, with about 90% tied to data centers.
why_it_matters: This stalls new grid connections right as hyperscalers race to lock up Texas power, adding schedule and financing risk to any project still awaiting interconnection. Expect a further push toward behind-the-meter and off-grid gas, storage and on-site generation deals as developers route around the freeze. Watch the August 20 PUCT meeting and whether the 90th Legislature moves in January 2027 to give PUCT permanent authority over data center approvals.
why_you_care: Any Texas data-center-linked power asset MSIP or a rival is underwriting now carries fresh interconnection timing risk that changes the deal calendar.

headline: Brightline Florida gets a sixth grace period on $1.2bn AAFOH bonds, 15th on commuter debt
players: Holders of Brightline's $1.2 billion unrated AAFOH tax-exempt bonds and $985 million commuter-linked bonds agreed to a seven-day grace period after the company again missed scheduled payments, per a July 31 notice on the MSRB's EMMA system. It's the sixth such supplement for the AAFOH bonds and the 15th for the commuter bonds.
why_it_matters: Brightline has now needed payment extensions on a near-monthly cadence for over a year, and the gap between grace periods keeps shrinking rather than stabilizing. Ridership is at record highs, but debt service and liquidity remain the binding constraint. Watch whether this cycle ends in a negotiated restructuring or a Chapter 11 filing, and whether the commuter rail financing structure survives intact.
why_you_care: This is the deal you underwrote at Rothschild; the extensions are becoming routine, which is itself a signal worth flagging on the restructuring timeline at MSIP.

headline: KKR closes largest-ever infrastructure fund at $19.2bn
players: KKR closed KKR Global Infrastructure Investors V at $19.2 billion, its largest infrastructure fund to date, targeting assets in North America and Western Europe. The fund has already committed over $9 billion across deals including Altitude III, EDF power solutions North America, Enilive, FiberCop, Global Technical Realty, Gulf Data Hub, Metronet and Sempra Infrastructure. Across its latest vintages, KKR has now raised roughly $45 billion for infrastructure globally.
why_it_matters: This is the biggest infrastructure fund close of the cycle and shows LPs still crowding into scale managers even as smaller shops struggle to hit targets. The seed portfolio — power, fiber and data infrastructure — signals where KKR sees the best risk-adjusted returns right now. Watch how fast the remaining roughly $10bn of dry powder gets deployed into power and digital deals.
why_you_care: KKR just banked its biggest-ever infrastructure war chest, a useful marker for what LPs will pay to back scale managers chasing the same power and digital deals MSIP competes for.
